messages:
Alex: quick sync — thinking about a lightweight decision-bus for canary/A-B rollouts so fallback triggers aren't walled off in one service. want to sketch tradeoffs.
Priya: +1. what do you mean by decision-bus? event stream with small policy agents?
Alex: yep — single pub/sub for rollout signals (latency, err-rate, quality-regressions) and tiny evaluation agents subscribe and emit actions (scale, divert, abort).
Sam: sounds promising. main worry: increased blast radius if bus becomes authoritative. how do we avoid conflicting actions?
Alex: design idea: actions carry a priority tuple (origin, score, ttl) and bus enforces a deterministic merge function. lower-priority actions can be ignored.
Jordan: deterministic merge is good. also need an escape hatch token that can force a safe fallback regardless of bus state (sheriff flow).
Taylor: we should also bound autoscale/divert frequency to avoid thrash. maybe a per-tenant rate limiter + cooldown window.
Priya: question: where do we evaluate quality regressions? at the observer (close to traffic) or centrally? observers can access raw payloads but we need privacy constraints.
Sam: prefer near-observer evals (less latency) but emit only aggregated signals to bus to respect PII.
Alex: agreed. observers emit "regression_score":0-100 and sample-count. bus computes weighted roll-forward metric.
Jordan: how does rollback quorum work? do we require multiple independent signals (err-rate + lat model-decay) to abort, or single catastrophic signal should be enough?
Taylor: pragmatic: allow configurable policy per-release. default: 1 catastrophic (500s/rate spike) OR 2 weak signals (latency + quality) within 5m.
Priya: can we express this policy as a small DSL? example: `when error_rate > 5% for 1m -> abort` or `when quality_drop > 12 & latency_p95 > 500ms -> reduce_traffic 50%`
Alex: yes — policy DSL stored alongside rollout config. bus evaluates compiled predicates in order. policies are versioned so rollback of policy is possible.
Sam: operational concern: how do we test this end-to-end? we need a shadow mode where actions are suggested but not executed, plus a dry-run reporter.
Jordan: add a "safety-audit" that logs suggested actions with hashes of inputs for replay testing.
deploy-bot: Deploy: canary v2.3 started in us-west-2 (10% traffic). link: https://console/redwood/deploys/2331 :rocket:
Taylor: perfect timing. let's run the new bus in observe-only mode for this canary. no automatic aborts yet.
Priya: timeline: observe-only for 24h, then opt-in to automated aborts for low-risk services, canary-specific policy TTLs.
Alex: followups: (1) sketch merge function and action priority, (2) policy DSL minimal grammar, (3) observer signal schema (aggregates only). I'll open an RFC draft.
Sam: I'll prototype a small simulator to validate quorum rules and cooldowns.
Jordan: I'll wire the escape hatch UI in ops console (manual override + provenance).
Taylor: I'll add rate-limiter hooks in the router to implement partial-divert.
Priya: sounds good. curious if we should add a cost-aware action (prefer cheaper fallback first) — worth a note in RFC.
Alex: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
